suppress.notes:
Copied from izgw-bom dependency-suppression.xml (develop, 1fc1f1a) on 2026-09-22 (IGDD-2396). Keep the two copies the same. The text that follows is the izgw-bom note, unchanged: "pom.xml" and "the protobuf-java note below" refer to izgw-bom. In izgw-hub this rule replaces five sha1-pinned rules for the same CVE, which stopped matching after the Spring Boot 4 upgrade.
spring-security-* (all versions): CVE-2018-1258 is an authorization bypass in method security that requires Spring Framework 5.0.5 specifically. NVD pins the vulnerable framework as cpe:2.3:a:vmware:spring_framework:5.0.5 — an exact version, not a range — while encoding the Spring Security side as cpe:2.3:a:pivotal_software:spring_security:*:*:*:*:*:*:*:* with no version bounds at all, because the CVE text reads "when used in combination with any versions of Spring Security". Dependency-Check therefore flags every spring-security JAR ever published, and no upgrade can clear it. This project ships spring-framework 7.0.9 (see spring-framework.version in pom.xml), so the vulnerable condition cannot occur.
GUARD: this suppression is valid only while spring-framework.version is not 5.0.5. If the framework is ever pinned to 5.0.5, remove this rule — the finding would be real.
Replaces six <sha1>-pinned rules covering spring-security-core/crypto at 6.5.9, 6.5.10 and 6.5.11 (added 2026-04-17 through 2026-06-11). Because the CPE is version-wildcard, each Spring Security release produced a fresh false positive and needed a new sha1 rule; all six went stale at once on the Boot 4 upgrade and logged "Suppression Rule had zero matches" in publish run 35104733706, letting the finding fail the --failOnCVSS 7 gate. Matching by filePath regex ends that treadmill and covers sibling artifacts (web, config, oauth2, ...) that carry the same product-level CPE. Scope stays narrow in the dimension that matters: only CVE-2018-1258 is suppressed, so any other CVE on any spring-security JAR still fails the build.
filePath+cve is the matcher shape known to work in this configuration; <packageUrl> and version-agnostic <cpe> were both verified not to match here (see the protobuf-java note below re: --disableCentral and PURL-less JARs). Added: 2026-09-16 (IGDD-2353)

tomcat-embed-core: CVE-2026-66299 is a false positive for embedded Tomcat usage. The vulnerability is an unbounded buffer for undelivered messages in the WebSocket chat example web application bundled with the full Apache Tomcat distribution, allowing a slow client to exhaust memory. Apache's own advisory states users who removed the examples web application are not affected. Our use of tomcat-embed does not include the examples web application - this is Spring Boot's embedded Tomcat (tomcat-embed-core/-el/-websocket only, pulled in via izgw-bom's tomcat.version property), which never bundles the examples webapp in the first place. Confirmed as a known false-positive pattern on the Apache Tomcat security mailing list thread for this CVE.
Fixed versions (11.0.25 / 10.1.58 / 9.0.121) had not been released as of this writing - confirmed tomcat-embed-core 10.1.58 does not yet exist on Maven Central (still under development). Revisit once 10.1.58 ships; this suppression may become unnecessary (harmless if left in place - it will simply stop matching). Added: 2026-08-08 (IGDD-3254)
